items.title: Super Micro smuggling co-conspirator pleads guilty to sending AI chips to China
items.description: Ting-Wei "Willy" Sun, one of the three people charged of smuggling Super Micro servers with advanced Nvidia AI chips to China, has pleaded guilty, with sentencing set for September of next year.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun, a third-party broker and “fixer” who’s been charged alongside Super Micro co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw and sales manager Ruei-Tsang “Steven” Chang for conspiring to unlawfully divert Nvidia AI chips to China, has pleaded guilty to the allegations against him. According to Bloomberg, Sun’s plea comes as part of an agreement with prosecutors, although the details of any possible cooperation arrangement remain undisclosed. Sun is also expected to be sentenced on Sept. 8, 2027, after entering his plea.The case against the individuals was revealed earlier this year after it was discovered that they diverted Super Micro servers containing Nvidia chips to China. The three were reported to have sent the servers to a Southeast Asian company, which then proceeded to fake the paperwork and create dummy servers for inspectors. Workers then used hair dryers to remove the serial numbers on the real servers to transfer them to the dummy server shells to complete the illusion, while the real servers made their way to China. Further investigation revealed that the three used a Thailand-based corporation to receive the servers, which were then delivered to Alibaba, even as the Chinese tech giant denied receiving the banned Nvidia hardware.Super Micro has also denied any knowledge of the operation, even as it has netted $2.5 billion in sales since it started in 2024. Nevertheless, the company’s shareholders have sued it, accusing it of concealing its dependence on illicit sales to China. Liaw, on the other hand, has pleaded not guilty to the charges and was released on a $5 million bond. The Super Micro co-founder is set to go to trial this coming Nov. 2, even as the third co-conspirator, Chang, remains a fugitive.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Taiwanese authorities are also building their own case against the illegal shipment of AI chips to China, with the investigators raiding some Super Micro offices and the homes of six individuals. The company, on the other hand, denied that its premises were raided, insisting that it cooperated with the police and provided access to the workstations and gadgets of the employees that were being investigated. It also said that it has been collaborating with both U.S. and Taiwanese authorities over the smuggling investigation, and that it has even fired several employees after completing its own independent investigation. Soon after this, Taiwan indicted nine more people involved in the illegal smuggling of Nvidia B300 GPUs.Sun’s guilty plea is the latest development in the U.S.’s clampdown on illegal AI chip exports, which happened soon after another tech CEO was arrested in California for smuggling $300 million in Nvidia AI servers to China. These cases show how serious the White House is about protecting its hardware advantage over Beijing in the AI race, even as AI development is facing its own challenges at home. items.titleZh: Super Micro smuggling co-conspirator pleads guilty to sending AI chips to China
items.descriptionZh:
美国对华AI芯片出口管制执法再度出现关键进展。第三方经纪人和“中间人”孙廷伟（Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun）已就相关指控认罪。他被控与美超微（Super Micro）联合创始人廖益贤（Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw）以及销售经理张瑞仓（Ruei-Tsang “Steven” Chang）共谋，将受出口管制的英伟达AI芯片非法转运至中国。根据彭博社报道，孙廷伟的认罪属于与检方达成协议的一部分，但是否包含配合调查、指证其他被告等安排，目前尚未披露。他预计将于2027年9月8日宣判。

案件背景是，美国近年来不断收紧对华先进AI芯片出口，试图在人工智能竞赛中维持对中国的硬件优势。今年早些时候，这起案件被曝光：涉案人员被指向东南亚公司运送装有英伟达芯片的美超微服务器，再由该公司伪造文件，并为检查人员制作假服务器。具体手法相当隐蔽：工人用吹风机加热并移除真实服务器上的序列号标签，再将其贴到假服务器外壳上，以完成调包假象，而真正的服务器则被运往中国。进一步调查显示，三人利用一家位于泰国的公司接收服务器，随后将其交付给阿里巴巴。不过，阿里巴巴否认收到被禁止的英伟达硬件。

从所谓“技术原理”看，本案并不涉及芯片性能或架构创新，关键点在于规避出口管制的物流与欺诈手法：利用东南亚中转、伪造报关和检查材料、制作假服务器、转移序列号，从而让真实AI服务器在形式上“消失”并流入中国。这类手法针对的是海关和出口合规检查，而不是芯片本身的技术突破。涉案产品包括英伟达AI芯片及相关服务器，台湾方面后续案件还涉及英伟达B300 GPU，但新闻未披露具体算力、显存、互联带宽等性能参数。

在法律和商业层面，美超微否认对相关操作知情，但报道称该操作自2024年以来已带来25亿美元销售额。公司股东已起诉美超微，指控其隐瞒对中国非法销售的依赖。廖益贤对指控不认罪，并以500万美元保释，预计今年11月2日受审；第三名被告张瑞仓仍在逃。台湾当局也在构建自己的案件，调查人员曾突袭美超微部分办公室和六名个人住所。美超微否认办公室被突袭，称公司配合警方并提供被调查员工的工作站和设备访问权限，同时表示正与美国和台湾当局合作调查，并在完成独立调查后解雇数名员工。随后，台湾又起诉另外九名涉嫌非法走私英伟达B300 GPU的人员。孙廷伟认罪是美国打击非法AI芯片出口的最新进展。此前，加州一名科技公司CEO也因涉嫌向中国走私价值3亿美元的英伟达AI服务器被捕，最高可能面临20年监禁。

这些案件表明，美国白宫和执法机构正以刑事起诉、出口管制和供应链审查等方式，严防先进AI硬件流入中国。其技术影响和应用场景主要围绕AI数据中心、大模型训练与推理等高性能算力需求展开：英伟达AI芯片和集成GPU的服务器是当前AI基础设施的核心，因此成为出口管制和走私争夺的焦点。对相关企业而言，这意味着更严格的合规审计、序列号追踪、转口贸易审查和内部治理要求；对AI产业而言，则可能进一步加剧先进算力获取的地缘政治分化。

items.description: This week on Tom's Hardware Premium, we covered how the AI buildout is affecting the industry supporting it across all axioms, including in law, chip design, manufacturing, and finance.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter In case you've been missing out on the action over on Tom's Hardware Premium, we're back with another roundup to fill you in on everything you missed. Central to this week's theme is how Artificial Intelligence and its subsequent buildout are currently impacting all areas of the semiconductor industry.Headlining this week is our report on how smart software utilization may play a part in the electricity consumption of AI data centers. We sat down and talked with experts in the domain to find out.Software could be the easiest fix for hyperscalers' AI power squeeze, researchers say — data center demand is expected to rival Japan's electricity usage by 2030Reports state that Tencent has reached a deal to lease high-performance AI chips from Oracle to the tune of $7 billion over five years. While the figure on its surface sounds significant, the estimated lease price is around 43% less than an Nvidia H100 leased at $2.80 per hour on a one-year contract, meaning that Tencent may have scored a slight coup in the terms of its lease agreement. While no specific chips have been named, the size of the deal and the prices point toward a Hopper-class GPU. We explored how this rental loophole may be used by Chinese firms to potentially gain access to otherwise export-controlled hardware.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Tencent scores 100,000 offshore AI chip deal with Oracle for $7 billion despite climbing prices — per-hour costs estimated to be 43% under standard H100 rental ratesIf you cast your minds back to last week, Synopsys revealed a slew of new agreements and partnerships; one of the most notable among them was an agreement with OpenAI, unveiling a 'GPT-Synopsys' — a specialized AI model that leverages Synopsys' domain IP knowledge and EDA tools, with OpenAI's capability to design LLMs. GPT-Synopsys is, in all likelihood, a chipmaking-specialized AI model, which may play a part in the development of successors to OpenAI's Jalapeño AI ASIC. As we've previously explored, AI models designing chips will likely run into hurdles surrounding IP usage, which become a non-factor if both AI labs and IP holders decide to team up in a manner such as this, setting the stage for chip design's agentic future.OpenAI and Synopsys partner to build "GPT-Synopsys" for autonomous chip design — specialized AI model will operate EDA tools, allowing engineers to deliver more sophisticated chips fasterNeon is a noble gas that's widely used in the DUV chipmaking process, with over 70% of global supply being used by the now-older lithography machines. Crude neon production has usually been focused in Ukraine, and ever since the advent of the country's ongoing conflict with Russia, global supply has been disrupted. Now, companies are racing to bring neon gas recycling systems to market in order to make the most of supplies. Japanese lithography toolmaker Gigaphoton and rival Kanten Techno have both developed machines that recycle the material at varying degrees of success. While DUV lithography remains a primary focus for the Chinese chipmaking ecosystem, the material is not widely used in the newer EUV systems that many leading-edge nodes currently utilize. While the official announcement is light on detail and subject to approval, an additional report claims that Huawei's LogicFolding chip-stacking methods are also included in the deal, with products ranging across AI, networking, compute, and other technologies. What makes Huawei's LogicFolding approach so notable is that the technique follows and targets faster data transmission as a foil to not having access to the most advanced EUV machines. Additionally, many of the techniques that LogicFolding incorporates echo what others in the chip industry are already doing, which makes it an eyebrow-raising move on Qualcomm's part. Historically, patent licensing between the two companies has been on the other foot — Huawei licensing Qualcomm patents — not the other way around. We explore the deal in detail in our full article.Qualcomm will license patents behind Huawei’s LogicFolding chip architecture, report says — the Kirin 9050 Pro already uses it, with a teardown showing its lower die is mostly cache and I/OTwo former Groq employees and shareholders have filed a proposed class action lawsuit against Groq's former board and CEO, alleging that the company's board breached its duties and cost stockholders billions, following Groq's $20 billion deal with Nvidia in December 2025, according to a new report. The deal between Groq and Nvidia didn't involve an acquisition, and Nvidia is not a named defendant in the case, though the vast majority of Groq's staff have reportedly since joined Nvidia directly. The Groq3 LPU has since been showcased as a part of Nvidia's Vera Rubin ecosystem, which is currently ramping. The race towards building capable open-weight models has predominantly been dominated by either U.S. or Chinese labs, meaning a European breakthrough is significant. items.titleZh: 本周 Tom's Hardware 高级版：2026年10月10日
items.descriptionZh:
本周 Tom's Hardware Premium 周报围绕一个核心趋势展开：AI 的算力扩张正在同时改变芯片需求、设计方式、供应链、能源消耗和地缘政治格局。以下为本周重点内容。

**AI 数据中心电力瓶颈：软件优化或成最容易的突破口**  
随着 AI 数据中心规模迅速膨胀，电力供应正成为超大规模云厂商最紧迫的约束之一。研究人员指出，智能软件利用可能是缓解 AI 电力紧张最容易实现的方案。报告援引专家访谈称，到 2030 年，全球数据中心用电需求预计将可与日本全国用电量相匹敌。这意味着，除了新建电厂和电网，如何通过软件调度、负载编排、动态功耗管理和利用率优化来降低单位算力能耗，将成为 AI 基础设施竞争的关键环节。

**腾讯与 Oracle 达成 70 亿美元 AI 芯片租赁协议，或成出口管制“租赁漏洞”**  
报道称，腾讯已与 Oracle 达成协议，将在五年内租赁价值 70 亿美元的高性能 AI 芯片，涉及约 10 万颗芯片。虽然总金额巨大，但估算显示，其每小时租赁价格约为 1.6 美元，比 Nvidia H100 一年期合同每小时 2.80 美元的标准租金低约 43%。尽管协议未点名具体芯片型号，但交易规模和价格指向 Hopper 级 GPU。  
这一安排的关键背景是美国对华先进 AI 芯片出口管制。中国企业直接购买受控硬件受限，但通过海外云厂商租赁算力，可能形成规避管制的“租赁漏洞”。若该模式被广泛采用，中国 AI 公司可在境外获得先进训练和推理算力，同时 Oracle 等云厂商获得大额收入，但也会引发更严格的监管审查。该交易因此不仅是商业租赁，更涉及出口管制有效性和全球 AI 算力地缘政治。

**OpenAI 与 Synopsys 合作构建“GPT-Synopsys”，推动自主芯片设计**  
Synopsys 本周公布多项新协议，其中最受关注的是与 OpenAI 的合作：双方将推出“GPT-Synopsys”，一个结合 Synopsys 领域 IP 知识、EDA 工具与 OpenAI 大语言模型设计能力的专用 AI 模型。它很可能是面向芯片制造的专用 AI 模型，并可能参与 OpenAI“Jalapeño”AI ASIC 后继产品的开发。  
核心技术逻辑在于：AI 模型设计芯片通常会遇到 IP 使用和工具链权限的障碍；如果 AI 实验室与 IP/EDA 厂商合作，这些障碍可被消除。GPT-Synopsys 可操作 EDA 工具，帮助工程师更快交付更复杂的芯片，推动芯片设计走向“代理化”未来。其应用场景包括芯片架构探索、RTL 生成、验证、物理设计等 EDA 流程的自动化。

**氖气回收系统上线：DUV 光刻供应链的救生索**  
氖气是一种惰性气体，广泛用于 DUV 光刻工艺，全球超过 70% 的氖供应被较老的光刻机消耗。粗氖生产通常集中在乌克兰，俄乌冲突爆发后全球供应受到严重扰乱。为此，日本光刻工具制造商 Gigaphoton 与竞争对手 Kanten Techno 竞相推出氖气回收系统。Gigaphoton 声称其系统可实现 50% 的回收率。  
技术原理是从 DUV 设备废气中回收氖气，经过纯化后重新用于光刻激光气体混合物。由于 DUV 仍是中国芯片制造生态的主要依赖，而 EUV 对氖的需求相对有限，氖回收系统对依赖 DUV 的芯片制造商具有重要供应安全意义，可缓解供应链风险并降低材料成本。

**高通获华为 LogicFolding 芯片堆叠专利许可，专利关系历史性反转**  
报道称，高通已与华为达成协议，将获得华为 LogicFolding 芯片架构相关专利许可，交易还涵盖 AI、网络、计算等技术领域的产品。LogicFolding 是一种芯片堆叠方法，核心目标是实现更快的数据传输，作为无法获得最先进 EUV 光刻机的一种替代路径。其许多技术思路与芯片行业已有做法相似，但华为已将其用于 Kirin 9050 Pro，拆解显示其下层 die 主要是缓存和 I/O。  
这一交易引人注目之处在于历史性反转：过去两家公司的专利许可主要是华为向高通支付专利费，而此次是高通获得华为专利许可。若交易获批，说明先进封装和芯片堆叠技术在地缘政治限制下的战略价值进一步上升，也可能影响未来 AI、网络和计算芯片的设计路线。

**Groq 前员工起诉董事会：200 亿美元 Nvidia 交易引发股东诉讼**  
两名前 Groq 员工和股东对 Groq 前董事会及 CEO 提起拟议集体诉讼，指控董事会违反职责，在 2025 年 12 月 Groq 与 Nvidia 达成 200 亿美元交易后导致股东损失数十亿美元。该交易并非正式收购，Nvidia 也不是被告，但据报道，绝大多数 Groq 员工已直接加入 Nvidia。Groq3 LPU 已在 Nvidia Vera Rubin 生态中展示并正在爬坡，Nvidia 的 Groq 3 LPX 计划于 2026 年下半年随 Vera Rubin 出货。  
原告称，董事会实际上把 LPU 技术和团队交给了 Nvidia，却让其他股东未能分享数十亿美元价值。此案凸显 AI 芯片初创公司在与巨头进行“非收购式”人才和技术整合时的治理与法律风险。

**Mistral 发布万亿参数 Large 4：欧洲最佳，但仍落后中国开源模型**  
欧洲公司 Mistral 发布 Large 4，也称 ML4，社媒上称“Le Chonk”。这是一个万亿参数模型。开放权重模型竞赛长期由美国或中国实验室主导，因此欧洲推出有竞争力的模型具有标志意义。测试机构 Artificial Analysis 给 ML4 的总体智能指数为 38 分，表现尚可，但仍落后于多个中国模型，包括 Kimi K3（max）、GLM-5.3-Flash 和 MiMo-V2.6.Pro。  
不过，ML4 在网络安全任务上表现突出，仅少数模型超过它。总体来看，欧洲主权 AI 努力虽取得明显进展，仍在追赶中国开源模型。Mistral 预计将在 10 月底前发布 ML4 的精确权重，全球闭源与开放权重模型的竞赛仍将继续。

综合来看，本周新闻共同显示：AI 已不只是芯片的应用场景，而是重塑芯片设计、制造、供应链、能源和法律格局的核心变量。

items.title: Senate investigation says that some AI data center claims are misleading
items.description: A Senate investigation on AI data centers question that costs and benefits that AI hyperscalers show when they apply for permits to put up their developments. The report says that these claims are misleading and that they don't show the real impact of these sites on the local economy.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 6 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The U.S. Senate has been conducting a year-long investigation into AI data centers, and its findings suggest that some developers have been misleading the public about the costs and benefits that these projects bring to their communities. According to Time, data center developers have routinely pointed to the number of construction jobs that projects bring to neighborhoods, but many have allegedly refused to share the number of permanent positions these projects bring to the neighborhood once they’ve reached operational status. A few companies that did give numbers point to a ratio of one permanent position for every megawatt of capacity, meaning a 100-megawatt development, which consumes around the same amount of electricity as 100,000 homes, would only hire 100 people.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsible“Congress must hold Big Tech accountable so these companies pay their fair share,” Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) told the publication. Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) also said, “This report lays bare what we have long known: working Americans and local communities are footing the bill for Big Tech’s massive expansion of data centers, while these companies continue to operate without transparency.”Aside from the lack of permanent jobs, the authorities also looked at the tax incentives these companies have been getting from local and state governments. The investigation revealed that although property-tax breaks catch critics’ attention during the application process, sales-tax exemptions on computer equipment are reportedly more lucrative, especially as these sites maintain, replace, and upgrade their hardware. The report estimated that 39% of a 1GW data center’s spending is allocated towards expensive GPUs, so if the data centers do not deliver the jobs and economic benefits they’ve promised, then the state is losing out on a lot of revenue.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The investigation also revealed that the surveyed companies — Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, CoreWeave, Digital Realty, and Equinix — don’t want to cover the costs of the additional infrastructure needed to serve their data centers even though they previously promised to “pay their own way.” While the companies said that they were willing to pay for direct costs, they argued that they should not be responsible for the larger investments that could potentially benefit other customers, such as new power plants and transmission lines, even though these were primarily driven by their power demands.There have already been efforts to legislate the ratepayer protection pledge that data center developers signed earlier this year, but it has failed because senators thought that it was “toothless.” This investigation shows that Congress is not giving up and that it’s conducting an even broader effort to regulate the infrastructure behind AI, especially with regard to its massive power consumption and other issues that residents living around them have been protesting against. items.titleZh: 参议院调查称部分AI数据中心的说法具有误导性
items.descriptionZh:
美国参议院一项为期一年的AI数据中心调查发现，一些开发商在项目给社区带来的成本与收益上误导公众。据Time报道，开发商通常大力宣传项目建设期创造的建筑岗位，却拒绝披露数据中心投入运营后能带来多少永久岗位。少数给出数据的公司显示：每1兆瓦容量仅对应约1个永久职位。也就是说，一个100兆瓦的数据中心——耗电量约相当于10万户家庭——只会雇用约100人。按此比例推算，1吉瓦项目也仅约1000个永久岗位。参议员Elizabeth Warren表示，国会必须问责大型科技公司，让它们支付公平份额；参议员Chris Van Hollen也指出，报告揭示了美国工薪阶层和地方社区正在为大型科技公司数据中心的巨大扩张买单，而这些公司却继续在缺乏透明度的情况下运营。

从技术与经济机制看，AI数据中心以大量GPU服务器为核心，训练和推理带来极高功耗，且需要冷却、变电和输电等配套基础设施。本次调查的核心并非芯片或算法创新，而是AI基础设施扩张中的成本转移与政策套利问题。调查除就业外，还审查了地方和州政府给予数据中心的税收优惠。申请阶段，房产税减免往往更引人关注，但针对计算机设备的销售税豁免实际上更有利，因为数据中心会持续维护、更换和升级硬件。报告估计，1吉瓦数据中心支出的39%用于昂贵GPU。如果这些项目未兑现就业和经济收益承诺，州政府将损失大量税收收入。

被调查公司包括Amazon、Google、Meta、Microsoft、CoreWeave、Digital Realty和Equinix。它们不愿承担服务数据中心所需的额外基础设施成本，尽管此前曾承诺“自付其路”。这些公司表示愿意支付直接成本，但认为不应为可能惠及其它用户的大型投资负责，例如新建发电厂和输电线路；然而这些投资主要由其电力需求驱动。今年早些时候，数据中心开发商签署的“费率payer保护承诺”曾试图立法，但因参议员认为其“没有牙齿”而失败。此次调查表明，国会并未放弃，而是对AI背后的基础设施展开更广泛监管，尤其针对其巨大电力消耗以及周边居民抗议等问题。相关趋势还包括：美国已有500多个AI数据中心禁令或限制、42个州发生142起抗议，亚马逊还警告680亿美元受阻数据中心威胁美国AI领先地位。整体来看，AI数据中心正从技术扩张问题演变为电力、税收、社区和监管的公共政策冲突；未来项目需要在选址、供电、成本分摊、税收透明和社区收益方面给出更可信承诺，否则可能面临更严格审查和部署阻力。

items.title: We tested gaming performance in 17-year-old Windows 7 on a modern gaming PC against Windows 11
items.description: We managed to install Windows 7 on a modern PC and put it to the test across eight DirectX 11 games and two DirectX 9 titles to see how its gaming performance compares to Windows 11 today.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 20 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter After the rough reception of Windows Vista, Windows 7 launched in 2009 to largely positive reviews. Even 17 years later, it remains one of the most beloved versions of Windows ever released. But how does this nearly two-decade-old operating system hold up on modern hardware? We managed to install Windows 7 on a modern PC and put it to the test across eight DirectX 11 games and two DirectX 9 titles to see how its gaming performance compares to Windows 11 today. Surprisingly, Windows 7 still carves out many notable wins over its successor.At launch, Windows 7 was very similar to Windows Vista in many respects. Vista had introduced significant changes under the hood compared to Windows XP, including technologies such as SuperFetch, ReadyBoost, ReadyDrive, new asynchronous APIs, and other I/O improvements. It also introduced native processor power management and various memory-management enhancements. On the visual side, Vista was the first version of Windows to feature Windows Aero, with its distinctive glass-like window borders.Windows 7 retained many of these underlying technologies while addressing several of Vista’s biggest criticisms. One notable improvement was greater control over User Account Control (UAC), allowing users to adjust how frequently they received UAC prompts. In Vista, these prompts could appear far too often, becoming a major source of frustration for many users.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Windows 7 also benefited from something that had nothing to do with the operating system itself: more powerful hardware. When Vista launched, many mid-range and budget PCs struggled to deliver smooth performance, particularly when using more demanding visual features such as Windows Aero. By 2009, however, PC hardware had advanced considerably, and the performance required to run these features smoothly was no longer a significant concern for most users.The Challenge of Running Windows 7 on a Modern PCGetting Windows 7 running on modern hardware is not as straightforward as installing a current version of Windows. At 17 years old, the operating system predates many of the technologies used by modern PCs, meaning driver support is extremely limited. For example, Windows 7 does not include native NVMe or USB 3.0 support, so the necessary drivers have to be slipstreamed into the installation ISO. Microsoft did eventually release patches that added NVMe support, but without injecting the appropriate drivers into the ISO, the Windows 7 installer will not recognize an NVMe drive. You may like We tested the impact of SSD speed on gaming performance in 11 titles Gears of War: E-Day PC graphics performance tested Gears of War E-Day is an uncharacteristically CPU-heavy Unreal Engine 5 game Our system is based on AMD’s AM5 platform (with the full system specifications detailed later in the article), which presents another limitation: there are no official Windows 7 chipset drivers for the platform.Fortunately, we are using an RDNA 2 GPU, which does have Windows 7 driver support, allowing us to use a relatively modern graphics card for our testing.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsThe motherboard is also an important consideration. Modern motherboards that have dropped CSM (Compatibility Support Module) and legacy boot support can make installing Windows 7 considerably more difficult, and in some cases may prevent the operating system from booting altogether. Fortunately, our motherboard still supports CSM, so this was not an issue for our setup.Test System (Image credit: Tom's Hardware)Windows 7 system specsAMD Radeon RX 6950 XTRyzen 7 9800X3D64GB (2x32GB) G.SKILL Flare X5 DDR5 @6000 MHz CL30Seagate Lightsaber FireCuda (530) NVMe SSDASUS ROG STRIX B850-F Gaming WiFiCorsair Nautilus 360 RS AIO CoolerHAGS not supported by driverWindows 7 Ultimate 64-bit Service Pack 1 (Build 7601)AMD Adrenalin 22.6.1 for Windows 7 (2022)Windows 11 system specsAMD Radeon RX 6950 XTRyzen 7 9800X3D64GB (2x32GB) G.SKILL Flare X5 DDR5 @6000 MHz CL30Seagate Lightsaber FireCuda (530) NVMe SSDASUS ROG STRIX B850-F Gaming WiFiCorsair Nautilus 360 RS AIO CoolerHAGS not supported by driverWindows 11 25H2 (Build 26200.9278)AMD Adrenalin 22.6.1 for Windows 11 (2022)For Windows 7, we disabled Secure Boot, enabled CSM, and set Boot Device Control to Legacy OPROM Only. Enabling CSM means that we no longer have access to Resizable BAR (it's not supported anyway). For Windows 11, we disabled VBS (Virtualization-Based Security) and HVCI (Hypervisor-Protected Code Integrity).It is important to note that while we used Adrenalin 22.6.1 for both Windows 11 and Windows 7 testing, the two packages contain different internal driver versions. Although both packages were released in June 2022, the Windows 11 driver is based on a more advanced codebase than the Windows 7 driver. What to read next Control Resonant PC performance tested Benchmarking 31 different CPUs in Onimusha: Way of the Sword AMD Ryzen 7 7700X3D review: A slower 7800X3D, but not necessarily a cheaper one In both cases, we performed a clean install of each operating system and filled the SSD to about 50-60%.Performance TestingWe tested ten games in total: eight using DirectX 11 and two using DirectX 9. The DirectX 11 titles are the primary focus, as both systems support them natively. By comparison, our Windows 11 system will run DirectX 9 games through the D3D9On12 mapping layer, while our Windows 7 system will run them natively. There are ways to get around the use of D3D9On12 on Windows 11, but we want to evaluate the out-of-the-box experience that most gamers would encounter. As a result, we expect Windows 7 to have an advantage in the DirectX 9 titles.It will become apparent in the results below that the advantages of each operating system will vary depending on whether we are CPU-limited or GPU-limited.Metro 2033 Redux (DX11)Metro 2033 Redux was released in 2014 and features a new lighting engine, higher visual fidelity, and new locations for certain levels. The game is predominantly GPU-bound, but there are moments when GPU utilization drops sharply as you traverse the game world. At these points, the CPU becomes the limiting factor, resulting in a corresponding drop in performance. Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 3 View Original Image 2 of 3 View Original Image 3 of 3 View Original Although Windows 11 delivers a higher average frame rate, Windows 7 handles the CPU-related performance drops much better, resulting in significantly stronger 1% lows. Installing the AMD chipset drivers and enabling Resizable BAR improves 1% lows on Windows 11 slightly, but it still falls well behind Windows 7.Windows 11’s more advanced graphics driver appears to provide an advantage in GPU-limited scenarios, while Windows 7’s lower CPU overhead offers more consistent frame pacing, though with lower peak performance.Batman: Arkham Origins (DX11)Batman: Arkham Origins runs on a modified version of Unreal Engine 3 and uses several DX11 enhancements such as Tessellation, Ambient Occlusion HBAO+, Percentage Closer Soft Shadows (PCSS), and Depth of Field (DoF). Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 3 View Original Image 2 of 3 View Original Image 3 of 3 View Original When CPU-limited at 1080p, Windows 7 once again puts in a strong showing, outperforming Windows 11 in both average frame rate and 1% lows. Surprisingly, Windows 7 also comes out ahead at 4K in Origins, though with a far smaller advantage. As we will see throughout the remainder of our testing, however, this is a rare occurrence. Even so, Windows 7 maintains a slight performance advantage over Windows 11 at 4K in this title.Batman: Arkham Knight (DX11)Batman: Arkham Knight was both a critical and commercial success, despite a notoriously troubled PC launch plagued by severe bugs and major performance issues. Visually, however, the game still holds up remarkably well, and modern hardware is more than capable of brute-forcing this demanding PC port. Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 3 View Original Image 2 of 3 View Original Image 3 of 3 View Original Windows 7 again delivers higher performance at 1080p when we are CPU-limited. Windows 11 jumps ahead when we become GPU-limited at 1440p and 4K.Batman: Arkham City (DX11)Batman: Arkham City was the second entry in the series, following Arkham Asylum, and the first to support DirectX 11. This introduced features such as tessellation, which adds greater geometric detail to characters and environments. Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 3 View Original Image 2 of 3 View Original Image 3 of 3 View Original In Arkham City, our system is GPU-bound at every resolution tested, giving Windows 11 the advantage across the board.The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt (DX11)The Witcher 3 faced some controversy at launch over reductions in image quality compared to its initial reveal. CD Projekt Red quickly released a patch addressing these concerns and improving the game’s visuals. From a performance perspective, however, the game was extremely demanding at launch. Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 3 View Original Image 2 of 3 View Original Image 3 of 3 View Original While the game is very GPU bound in general, at 1080p we did encounter a slight CPU bottleneck, which gave Windows 7 an advantage in 1% lows. At 1440p and 4K, Windows 11 takes a slight lead.Control (DX11)Control is the newest title we tested for this comparison, having launched in 2019. While the game introduced several ray tracing features, these were exclusive to the DirectX 12 API. Since Windows 7 does not support DirectX 12, we tested Control using DirectX 11 on both operating systems. Even without ray tracing, Control remains the most graphically advanced title in our Windows 11 vs Windows 7 comparison. Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 3 View Original Image 2 of 3 View Original Image 3 of 3 View Original Windows 11 wins across the board. This is not a surprise, as we are GPU-limited across all resolutions tested.Hitman: Absolution (DX11)Hitman: Absolution was released in 2012 and was the first game to use the Glacier 2 engine. The updated engine could handle crowds of up to 1200 characters, which was unprecedented at the time. The game also featured several DirectX 11 enhancements, including global illumination and tessellation. Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 3 View Original Image 2 of 3 View Original Image 3 of 3 View Original This is another game that pushes the GPU hard, regardless of resolution. Our test system was GPU-limited even at 1080p.Hitman 2 (DX11)Hitman 2 was released in 2018, making it the second-newest game in our operating system comparison. It features detailed environments, dense crowds, and full reflections across many surfaces, making it an impressive-looking title overall. Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 3 View Original Image 2 of 3 View Original Image 3 of 3 View Original Hitman 2 is another example where our test system is GPU-limited at every resolution, giving Windows 11 a clean sweep across the board.Batman: Arkham Asylum (DX9)We now move to our first DirectX 9 game. As previously mentioned, Windows 7 should have an advantage here because our Windows 11 system must use the D3D9On12 mapping layer for DirectX 11 games. But just how much of an advantage? Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 3 View Original Image 2 of 3 View Original Image 3 of 3 View Original Significant advantages for Windows 7 in average frame rate and 1% lows, especially at 1080p and 1440p. The advantage is reduced at 4K, but the performance is still smoother overall in Windows 7. Another translation layer, such as DXVK, may close the gap.Borderlands 2 (DX9)Borderlands 2 is our second DirectX 9 game and the final overall game tested. Image 1 of 3 (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) Image 1 of 3 View Original Image 2 of 3 View Original Image 3 of 3 View Original Once again, another massive win for Windows 7 at the lower resolutions. The performance at 4K is virtually identical.Bottom LineWindows 11 is optimized for GPU-hungry gamesThe results are interesting, but perhaps not entirely surprising. The DirectX 9 results are largely in line with our expectations, given that Windows 11 must run these games through the D3D9On12 mapping layer, yielding substantial advantages for Windows 7.The DirectX 11 results are more nuanced, but a clear trend emerges: Windows 7 has the advantage when we are CPU-limited, while Windows 11 performs better when we are GPU-limited. This makes sense given that Windows 11 uses graphics drivers built on a more advanced codebase, while Windows 7 is a leaner operating system with fewer background processes and, consequently, lower CPU overhead.Microsoft has recently detailed its K2 plan, which aims to improve the performance and reliability of Windows 11. We hope these continued efforts to improve Windows 11 pay off.The lower CPU performance we observed in Windows 11 cannot be attributed to its most notable security features, such as VBS (Virtualization-Based Security) and HVCI (Hypervisor-Protected Code Integrity), as we disabled both during testing. Notably, Windows 7 does not support VBS or HVCI at the software level, while Windows 11 supports hardware virtualization extensions (such as Intel VT-x or AMD-V) and Second Level Address Translation (SLAT). Additionally, fixed-function hardware can reduce the impact of virtualization to varying degrees, based on the CPU architecture's capabilities. However, additional telemetry and other background services still pop up and use precious CPU cycles.Using the latest chipset drivers and enabling features such as Resizable BAR does not help Windows 11 close the gap in CPU-limited scenarios by any significant margin. Ultimately, we would like to see Windows 11 become leaner and more efficient, as our results suggest there is still some performance left on the table, particularly on the CPU side.

items.titleZh: 我们在现代游戏电脑上测试了17年前的Windows 7与Windows 11的游戏性能对比
items.descriptionZh:
Tom's Hardware 近日进行了一项颇具怀旧色彩但技术意义很强的测试：把 2009 年发布、至今仍被许多人视为经典且备受喜爱的 Windows 7 安装到现代 PC 上，并与 Windows 11 进行游戏性能对比。文章的核心问题是：在 Vista 口碑不佳之后推出的 Windows 7，虽然已近 17 年历史，但它在当代硬件上的游戏表现究竟如何？测试覆盖 8 款 DirectX 11 游戏和 2 款 DirectX 9 游戏，结果显示 Windows 7 在不少场景中仍能战胜 Windows 11，尤其是在 CPU 受限时。

文章先回顾了背景。Windows 7 在发布时与 Vista 在内核和底层技术上有很多相似之处。Vista 相比 Windows XP 引入了 SuperFetch、ReadyBoost、ReadyDrive、新的异步 API、I/O 改进、原生处理器电源管理以及多项内存管理增强，还首次带来 Windows Aero 玻璃特效界面。Windows 7 保留了这些底层技术，同时修正了 Vista 最受诟病的问题之一：用户账户控制 UAC 提示过于频繁。Windows 7 允许用户调整 UAC 提示频率，从而缓解了体验痛点。此外，Windows 7 的成功也得益于时代红利：到 2009 年，PC 硬件性能已大幅提升，运行 Aero 等较高要求特性不再像 Vista 时代那样吃力。

但要在现代 PC 上运行 Windows 7 并不容易。该系统原生不支持 NVMe 和 USB 3.0，必须把相应驱动 slipstream 注入安装 ISO；微软后来虽发布过 NVMe 支持补丁，但若不注入驱动，Windows 7 安装程序仍无法识别 NVMe 硬盘。测试使用的 AMD AM5 平台也没有官方 Windows 7 芯片组驱动。幸运的是，测试所用的 RDNA 2 显卡仍有 Windows 7 驱动支持。主板方面，现代主板若取消 CSM 和传统引导支持，可能导致 Windows 7 无法安装甚至无法启动；测试主板仍支持 CSM，因此可以继续。测试平台为：AMD Radeon RX 6950 XT、Ryzen 7 9800X3D、64GB DDR5-6000 CL30、Seagate FireCuda 530 NVMe SSD、ASUS ROG STRIX B850-F Gaming WiFi、Corsair Nautilus 360 RS AIO。Windows 7 使用 Ultimate 64-bit SP1 Build 7601 和 AMD Adrenalin 22.6.1 for Windows 7；Windows 11 使用 25H2 Build 26200.9278 和 AMD Adrenalin 22.6.1 for Windows 11。两个驱动包虽然都发布于 2022 年 6 月，但内部驱动版本不同，Windows 11 驱动基于更先进的代码库。测试中，Windows 7 关闭 Secure Boot、启用 CSM，并将 Boot Device Control 设为 Legacy OPROM Only，因此无法使用 Resizable BAR；Windows 11 则关闭了 VBS 和 HVCI。两者均为干净安装，SSD 填充约 50% 至 60%。

测试方法上，DirectX 11 游戏是重点，因为两套系统都原生支持。DirectX 9 游戏则不同：Windows 7 原生运行，Windows 11 必须通过 D3D9On12 映射层运行，因此预期 Windows 7 在 DX9 中占优。结果显示，性能差异主要取决于测试是 CPU 受限还是 GPU 受限。

在 DirectX 11 游戏中，《地铁2033 Redux》大部分时间受 GPU 限制，但穿越场景时会出现 GPU 利用率骤降、CPU 成为瓶颈。Windows 11 平均帧率更高，但 Windows 7 对 CPU 相关掉帧处理更好，1% lows 显著更强；安装 AMD 芯片组驱动并启用 Resizable BAR 后，Windows 11 的 1% lows 略有改善，但仍明显落后。《蝙蝠侠：阿卡姆起源》在 1080p CPU 受限时，Windows 7 的平均帧率和 1% lows 都超过 Windows 11；4K 下 Windows 7 也略占优势，但幅度很小，这在此次测试中较为罕见。《蝙蝠侠：阿卡姆骑士》在 1080p CPU 受限时 Windows 7 更高，1440p 和 4K 转为 GPU 受限后 Windows 11 反超。《蝙蝠侠：阿卡姆之城》在所有测试分辨率下都受 GPU 限制，Windows 11 全面领先。《巫师3：狂猎》总体非常依赖 GPU，1080p 下出现轻微 CPU 瓶颈，Windows 7 的 1% lows 更好；1440p 和 4K 下 Windows 11 略占上风。《控制》是测试中最新游戏，2019 年发布，但光追仅限 DirectX 12，而 Windows 7 不支持 DX12，因此两套系统均用 DX11 测试；由于所有分辨率都受 GPU 限制，Windows 11 全面获胜。《杀手：赦免》即使 1080p 也受 GPU 限制，因此 Windows 11 占优。《杀手2》在所有分辨率下都受 GPU 限制，Windows 11 同样全面领先。

DirectX 9 结果基本符合预期。《蝙蝠侠：阿卡姆疯人院》中，Windows 7 在平均帧率和 1% lows 上优势明显，尤其在 1080p 和 1440p；4K 下优势缩小，但整体仍更平滑。文章指出，若使用 DXVK 等其他翻译层，差距可能缩小。《无主之地2》中，Windows 7 在较低分辨率再次大幅领先，4K 下两者表现几乎相同。

最终结论是：Windows 11 更适合 GPU 吃重的游戏，而 Windows 7 在 CPU 受限场景中表现更好。DX9 结果主要因为 Windows 11 必须经过 D3D9On12 映射层，Windows 7 原生运行，因此优势明显。DX11 的趋势则更微妙：Windows 7 在 CPU 受限时领先，Windows 11 在 GPU 受限时领先。原因在于 Windows 11 使用基于更先进代码库的图形驱动，而 Windows 7 系统更精简、后台进程更少，CPU 开销更低。文章强调，Windows 11 较低的 CPU 性能不能归咎于 VBS 和 HVCI，因为测试中两者均已关闭；Windows 7 在软件层面不支持 VBS/HVCI，而 Windows 11 支持硬件虚拟化扩展和 SLAT，固定功能硬件可在不同程度上降低虚拟化开销，但额外的遥测和其他后台服务仍会占用宝贵 CPU 周期。使用最新芯片组驱动和启用 Resizable BAR 也不能显著缩小 Windows 11 在 CPU 受限场景中的差距。文章最后提到，微软近期公布了旨在提升 Windows 11 性能和可靠性的 K2 计划，作者希望这些努力能够奏效，并认为 Windows 11 仍有性能潜力可挖，尤其是在 CPU 侧，应变得更精简、更高效。该测试的意义在于揭示操作系统开销、驱动优化和翻译层对现代游戏性能的持续影响，同时也说明在新硬件上运行旧系统虽可行，但安装复杂且存在安全与兼容性限制，并不适合作为日常使用方案。

items.title: Nvidia reportedly halts GeForce RTX 5090 production in favor of AI data center and professional GPUs
items.description: Nvidia reportedly discontinues GeForce RTX 5090-series products leaving GB202 for data center and professional graphics boards. GeForce RTX 5080 24 GB rumored to become de-facto flagship from the green camp for a while.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 10 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Nvidia has reportedly ceased selling its GB202 graphics processors for consumer-grade GeForce RTX 5090-series add-in-boards (AIBs), including 'D' variants for the Chinese market, according to a leaked notice from an unknown factory cited by @hongxing2020, who tends to have insights into the graphics card market. Another prominent leaker @Zed__Wang confirmed the report and said that from now on the GB202 silicon will be exclusively used on data center and professional graphics cards."According to a notification from the factory, Nvidia will no longer manufacture any RTX 5090 models, including the D variants," a message cited by @hongxing2020 reads. "Going forward, the highest-end GeForce graphics card will be the RTX 5080 24GB, while the RTX 5080 16GB version will be discontinued. Please spread the word."This is, of course, an unverified claim and not an official Nvidia announcement. We asked Nvidia for a comment, though the company has yet to respond. Typically, Nvidia does not comment on rumors.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: While the information is strictly unofficial for now, the alleged decision would make considerable economic sense for Nvidia, as the company can sell GB202 processors on data center and professional graphics cards that cost substantially more than the GeForce RTX 5090. In fact, Nvidia's recently introduced RTX Pro 5500 features the same number of CUDA cores — 21,760 — as the GeForce RTX 5090, but comes with 84GB of GDDR7 memory instead of 32GB and targets considerably more lucrative professional visualization (ProViz) and AI applications. Meanwhile, the fully-fledged RTX 6000 Pro with 24,064 CUDA cores and 96 GB of memory can easily sell for $15,000.By discontinuing GB202-based GeForce products, Nvidia could prevent its relatively inexpensive consumer graphics cards from competing with its own professional accelerators in the lucrative AI sector. Essentially, the company is redirecting its limited semiconductor manufacturing allocation toward higher-margin products without necessarily sacrificing its position in the gaming market, as neither the GeForce RTX 5080 nor RTX 5090 have direct rivals. You may like Nvidia's RTX 5090 vanishes from online retail in the US Nvidia's fastest graphics cards get US price increase at Best Buy, Amazon Gaming takes a backseat as Nvidia overhauls the RTX 5090 for maximum AI margins Even if Nvidia has indeed discontinued shipments of GB202 processors for consumer graphics cards, GeForce RTX 5090 boards are unlikely to disappear from the market overnight. Nvidia's add-in-board partners, distributors, and retailers likely have inventories of GPUs and finished graphics cards that could sustain availability for some time. However, if Nvidia no longer supplies GB202 processors for GeForce products, the availability of RTX 5090 cards will inevitably decline, which will affect prices of these AIBs.Meanwhile, Nvidia could be preparing to refresh its GeForce RTX 50-series lineup. The company has long been rumored to be developing GeForce RTX 50 Super graphics cards, including an RTX 5080 Super with 24GB of GDDR7 memory, although their introduction has reportedly been postponed due to memory supply constraints. The rumored GeForce RTX 5080 24GB could therefore represent a revival of these plans, and with no more GeForce RTX 5090 32GB on the market, the new product will have better memory supply.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsNvidia is also developing its next-generation Rubin-based GeForce RTX 60-series GPUs, but recent rumors suggest that these products will not arrive until late 2027, or even 2028. Consequently, if the reports about the discontinuation of the GeForce RTX 5090 are accurate, Nvidia could leave the enthusiast gaming market without a GB202-class flagship for a considerable period, so if you are in the market for the absolute best graphics card, now is the time to get it. items.titleZh: Nvidia reportedly halts GeForce RTX 5090 production in favor of AI data center and professional GPUs
items.descriptionZh:
据泄露消息，Nvidia据称已停止向消费级GeForce RTX 5090系列显卡（AIB，即第三方板卡）供应GB202图形处理器，其中包括面向中国市场的“D”版本。该消息来自@hongxing2020引用的一份未知工厂通知，另一位知名爆料者@Zed__Wang也确认了该说法，并表示今后GB202硅片将专用于数据中心和专业显卡。泄露通知称，Nvidia将不再生产任何RTX 5090型号，包括D版本；未来最高端的GeForce显卡将是RTX 5080 24GB，而RTX 5080 16GB版本将被停产。目前这仍是非官方、未经证实的说法，Nvidia尚未回应Tom's Hardware的置评请求，且该公司通常不评论传闻。

从产品背景看，GB202是Nvidia Blackwell架构中面向消费级市场的顶级GPU，用于GeForce RTX 5090，配备21760个CUDA核心和32GB GDDR7显存。与之对比，Nvidia近期推出的RTX Pro 5500专业卡同样拥有21760个CUDA核心，但显存高达84GB GDDR7，面向专业可视化（ProViz）和AI应用；更高端的RTX 6000 Pro则拥有24064个CUDA核心和96GB显存，售价可轻松达到15000美元。核心技术逻辑在于：同一颗大芯片可以通过不同显存容量、驱动认证和产品定位，分割为消费级游戏卡与高利润专业/AI加速卡。GB202若用于专业卡，单颗芯片所对应的整卡价值和利润率远高于RTX 5090。

因此，若该决策属实，对Nvidia而言具有明显的经济合理性。公司可以把有限的半导体制造产能、先进封装和GDDR7显存供应，优先分配给数据中心和专业显卡，从而避免价格相对较低的消费级RTX 5090在利润丰厚的AI市场中与自家专业加速器竞争。与此同时，GeForce RTX 5080和RTX 5090在消费级市场都没有直接竞争对手，Nvidia即便减少旗舰游戏卡供应，也未必会显著削弱其在游戏市场的地位。这更像是一次产品组合和产能分配的调整，而非技术上的退步。

市场影响方面，即使Nvidia真的停止向消费级显卡供应GB202，RTX 5090也不会一夜之间从市场上消失。AIB合作伙伴、分销商和零售商可能仍持有GPU芯片和成品显卡库存，足以维持一段时间。但如果Nvidia不再供应GB202给GeForce产品，RTX 5090的可用量将不可避免地下降，进而推高这些显卡的价格。对于需要顶级游戏或本地AI性能的用户来说，供应收紧可能意味着购买窗口正在缩小。

与此同时，Nvidia可能在准备更新GeForce RTX 50系列。长期以来有传闻称公司正在开发RTX 50 Super系列，包括配备24GB GDDR7的RTX 5080 Super，但因显存供应限制而被推迟。泄露中提到的RTX 5080 24GB，可能正是这些计划的复活；在RTX 5090 32GB退出后，新款24GB显卡在显存供应上也会更可行。Nvidia还在开发下一代基于Rubin架构的GeForce RTX 60系列，但近期传闻称要到2027年底甚至2028年才会推出。若RTX 5090停产消息准确，Nvidia可能让发烧级游戏市场在相当长时间内缺少GB202级别的旗舰产品。因此，如果用户确实需要当前最顶级的显卡，可能需要尽快入手。整体来看，该消息尚待官方或供应链进一步证实，但其反映出的趋势——Nvidia将更多高端GPU产能转向AI和专业市场——与当前行业方向一致。

items.title: Crazed modder straps 360mm AIO radiator to laptop, cuts temps to below 40 degrees
items.description: PC modder TrashBench attached a 360mm radiator and custom cooling to a laptop and gained up to 14% in performance at the cost of the definition of a laptop.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter YouTube hardcore PC modder TrashBench attached waterblocks, a water pump, and a 360mm radiator to a Metabox laptop with an Nvidia GTX 1060 and Intel Core i7-8750H. This Frankenstein’s monster of a laptop dropped a whole 60℃ on both the CPU and GPU during benchmarks and stress tests and gained an average of 14% after overclocking.TrashBench, a YouTuber popular for extreme PC modifications involving various watercooling solutions, decided to “fix” laptop cooling by taking a cut-up 360mm AIO from another project and plans to use it on the Metabox P950EP. Metabox is an Australian brand of laptops rebranded from Clevo, an ODM brand from Taiwan that often gets rebranded in various countries. TrashBench intends to use this laptop for his daughter to play Fortnite on.The modder intended to use the stock AIO pump along with a second waterblock for the CPU, but after testing whether it would be strong enough to push through a second block, TrashBench realized he would need a bigger pump. He also needed to use another waterblock since the new pump was a standalone one, unlike the waterblock and pump combo on an AIO.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Laptop Cooling Is Stupid. I Fixed It. - YouTube Watch On The waterblocks were mounted via a 3D-printed holder, then screwed down to the existing holes previously used for the stock heatpipe and blower cooler. More 3D-printed mounts were used to hold the radiator behind the screen of the laptop, but couldn’t be screwed in because the space between the screen and shell was too small. TrashBench reluctantly used Loctite 2-part epoxy to attach the radiator mount onto the laptop.That’s not all epoxy was used for, as he didn’t forget about the RAM and VRMs. A heatsink was attached to them, with thermal pads bringing the RAM level with the VRMs to use a single heatsink for each cluster. The VRMs had a dab of thermal paste and a spot of epoxy to keep the heatsink in place, making the modification permanent. You may like Strapping 11 fans and a 360mm AIO to an RTX 3080 sounds crazy until you see the 30°C temp drop Modder pumps liquid directly over bare GPU silicon via 3D-printed block Enthusiast mods GTX 1080 Ti with a dual-tower CPU cooler, sees up to 32°C reduction in temps After fully assembling everything and attaching the blocks, pump, and radiator with flexible clear tubes using screw hose clamps, TrashBench tested it for leaks. “I think we’re good,” he says, just before a few bubbles passed by.The laptop uses 19v, while the pump and fans use 12v, so a DC-DC step-down converter was soldered to the original blower fan’s electrical contacts. Unfortunately, the power source powers on as soon as the laptop is turned on, with no way to make them only turn on under load. So the modder used a toggle switch mounted to a 3D-printed plate, screwed onto the bottom shell that had a large gaping hole cut out of it to accommodate the pump and waterblocks.Stay On the Cutting Edge: Get the Tom's Hardware NewsletterGet Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.Contact me with news and offers from other Future brandsReceive email from us on behalf of our trusted partners or sponsorsTo allow the laptop to stand, a 3D-printed riser was screwed to the bottom and is the final touch to the build. As ridiculous as it looks, it impresses with its performance, averaging 60℃ below stock, with the CPU and GPU staying well below 40℃ under full load. (Image credit: TrashBench)Conservative but clear performance gains were seen after benchmarks, but with the amount of temperature overhead, TrashBench decided to see how much more he could get by overclocking, and it was worth it, as Forza Horizon 5 went from 75 FPS to 77, and then to 83 FPS after overclocking. items.titleZh: Crazed modder straps 360mm AIO radiator to laptop, cuts temps to below 40 degrees
items.descriptionZh:
硬核PC改装YouTuber TrashBench将水冷块、水泵和360mm冷排加装到一台Metabox笔记本上，该机配备Nvidia GTX 1060和Intel Core i7-8750H。这个“科学怪人”式改装在基准与压力测试中将CPU和GPU温度降低约60℃，超频后平均性能提升14%。TrashBench以极端水冷改装闻名，他利用另一个项目切下的360mm一体式水冷（AIO），计划用于Metabox P950EP。Metabox是澳大利亚品牌，产品由台湾ODM厂商Clevo贴牌。该笔记本打算给他女儿玩《堡垒之夜》。

改装中，他原想沿用AIO原装泵并加第二个水冷头，但测试发现泵推力不足，需要换更大独立泵；又因新泵为独立式，需另配水冷头。水冷头通过3D打印支架安装，并拧到原热管和鼓风散热器留下的孔位。冷排通过3D打印支架固定在屏幕后方，但屏幕与外壳间隙太小无法上螺丝，只能改用乐泰双组分环氧树脂粘接。RAM和VRM也加装散热片：用导热垫使RAM与VRM齐平，每组芯片共用一个散热片；VRM涂导热膏并用少量环氧固定散热片，使改装成为永久性改造。组装后他测试了泄漏，期间有少量气泡通过。

供电方面，笔记本为19V，而泵和风扇为12V，因此他将DC-DC降压转换器焊接到原鼓风风扇的电气触点上。但该电源随笔记本开机即通电，无法仅在高负载时启动，于是加装拨动开关，固定在3D打印板上并拧到底壳；底壳切出大孔以容纳泵和水冷块。底部还拧上3D打印垫脚，使笔记本能站立。

性能上，改装后平均比原装低60℃，CPU和GPU满载下均远低于40℃。由于温度余量巨大，TrashBench尝试超频，获得平均14%的性能提升；《极限竞速：地平线5》从75 FPS升至77 FPS，超频后进一步到83 FPS。尽管外观夸张，但效果显著。该改装展示了外置水冷对笔记本散热的巨大潜力，可释放超频空间，但代价是便携性丧失、不可逆的永久改装、复杂供电和3D打印结构，主要适合硬核DIY玩家，不具备量产实用性。

items.title: Ukrainian drones strike largest data center in Russia, multiple parts of 1.4 million square foot campus knocked offline
items.description: Following a Ukrainian drone strike on a D.C. in Sasovo, Russia, a Yandex facility in Kaluga has suffered a similar fate with multiple modules completely out of service.
items.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Hot on the heels of a Ukrainian drone strike on a Russian Yandex data center in Sasovo that caused a major outage, a Yandex facility in Kaluga has been struck in a similar fashion. The huge data center was so badly damaged that Russian state media admitted that multiple modules had been removed from service completely.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsibleUnited24 Media reports that the facility is located in Grabtsevo industrial park and was designed to be the largest Yandex data center in all of Russia. It only entered service in the second half of 2023, lasting three years before this incident.The Kaluga data center is a sprawling complex that covers around 1.4 million square feet (130,000 square meters). It's so vast that its 63-megawatt power capacity is around 50% higher than some other data centers owned by Yandex. With more than 3,800 server racks, it's perhaps easy to see why it became a target for Ukraine's drone operators. If, of course, the facility was the intended target for the attack — something yet to be confirmed.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: As for what all those server racks actually do, it's reported that Yandex's internal services are housed at the facility. It was ultimately built to allow Yandex to expand its cloud offering.It's as yet unclear how this drone strike is affecting everyday Russians, but the previous Sasovo strike also impacted Yandex Cloud. At the time, users reported problems with Yandex Mail, Disk, Documents, Pay, and Market despite Yandex claiming that key services remained up and running. items.titleZh: 乌克兰无人机袭击俄罗斯最大数据中心，占地140万平方英尺的园区多处下线
items.descriptionZh:
继乌克兰无人机袭击俄罗斯萨索沃Yandex数据中心并造成重大服务中断后，位于卡卢加的又一座Yandex数据中心遭到类似打击。据United24 Media报道，该设施位于Grabtsevo工业园，原本设计为Yandex在俄罗斯全境最大的数据中心。它于2023年下半年才投入使用，却在本次事件中严重受损。俄罗斯国家媒体塔斯社确认，“由于无人机袭击，卡卢加Yandex数据中心多个模块已完全停止运行”，说明攻击不是轻微故障，而是导致部分计算、存储或网络模块整体退出服务。

从规模看，卡卢加数据中心占地约13万平方米（约140万平方英尺），供电容量达63兆瓦，比Yandex部分其他数据中心高出约50%，拥有超过3800个服务器机架。该设施主要承载Yandex内部服务，并用于扩展Yandex Cloud云业务。正因其体量巨大，它成为无人机操作员的高价值潜在目标；不过原文也指出，该设施是否就是预定袭击目标尚未得到确认。

技术层面，这类超大型数据中心并非单一服务器，而是由服务器机架、供电配电、冷却系统、网络互联以及云调度和虚拟化平台共同组成。模块化设计原本用于隔离故障、便于扩容和维护，但物理打击可以直接破坏供电、冷却或网络环节，使多个模块同时离线。63兆瓦电力和3800多个机架意味着大量算力、存储和带宽资源；一旦模块停摆，云服务容量、冗余和故障转移能力都会承压。原文没有涉及具体AI芯片、能效创新或性能跑分，但数据中心是云服务和AI算力的物理底座，因此其受损会直接影响上层数字服务。

影响方面，目前尚不清楚此次袭击对普通俄罗斯用户的具体影响。但此前萨索沃数据中心遇袭已影响Yandex Cloud，用户报告Yandex Mail、Disk、Documents、Pay和Market出现问题，尽管Yandex声称关键服务仍在运行。相关推荐阅读还提到，Yandex数据中心曾容纳两台顶级超级计算机，这进一步说明其战略价值。对Yandex而言，最大数据中心模块下线可能拖慢其云扩展计划；对俄罗斯数字生态而言，则可能加剧服务中断和算力资源紧张。

更广背景是，俄乌冲突中数字基础设施正成为互相打击的目标。本文提到，俄罗斯导弹本月早些时候袭击了乌克兰一处设施，导致全球第二大种子追踪器下线。卡卢加事件是这一系列攻击的最新一例，凸显战时数据中心面临的物理安全、地理冗余、灾备和云服务连续性挑战。

history.title: Super Micro smuggling co-conspirator pleads guilty to sending AI chips to China
history.description: Ting-Wei "Willy" Sun, one of the three people charged of smuggling Super Micro servers with advanced Nvidia AI chips to China, has pleaded guilty, with sentencing set for September of next year.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun, a third-party broker and “fixer” who’s been charged alongside Super Micro co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw and sales manager Ruei-Tsang “Steven” Chang for conspiring to unlawfully divert Nvidia AI chips to China, has pleaded guilty to the allegations against him. According to Bloomberg, Sun’s plea comes as part of an agreement with prosecutors, although the details of any possible cooperation arrangement remain undisclosed. Sun is also expected to be sentenced on Sept. 8, 2027, after entering his plea.The case against the individuals was revealed earlier this year after it was discovered that they diverted Super Micro servers containing Nvidia chips to China. The three were reported to have sent the servers to a Southeast Asian company, which then proceeded to fake the paperwork and create dummy servers for inspectors. Workers then used hair dryers to remove the serial numbers on the real servers to transfer them to the dummy server shells to complete the illusion, while the real servers made their way to China. Further investigation revealed that the three used a Thailand-based corporation to receive the servers, which were then delivered to Alibaba, even as the Chinese tech giant denied receiving the banned Nvidia hardware.Super Micro has also denied any knowledge of the operation, even as it has netted $2.5 billion in sales since it started in 2024. Nevertheless, the company’s shareholders have sued it, accusing it of concealing its dependence on illicit sales to China. Liaw, on the other hand, has pleaded not guilty to the charges and was released on a $5 million bond. The Super Micro co-founder is set to go to trial this coming Nov. 2, even as the third co-conspirator, Chang, remains a fugitive.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: Taiwanese authorities are also building their own case against the illegal shipment of AI chips to China, with the investigators raiding some Super Micro offices and the homes of six individuals. The company, on the other hand, denied that its premises were raided, insisting that it cooperated with the police and provided access to the workstations and gadgets of the employees that were being investigated. It also said that it has been collaborating with both U.S. and Taiwanese authorities over the smuggling investigation, and that it has even fired several employees after completing its own independent investigation. Soon after this, Taiwan indicted nine more people involved in the illegal smuggling of Nvidia B300 GPUs.Sun’s guilty plea is the latest development in the U.S.’s clampdown on illegal AI chip exports, which happened soon after another tech CEO was arrested in California for smuggling $300 million in Nvidia AI servers to China. These cases show how serious the White House is about protecting its hardware advantage over Beijing in the AI race, even as AI development is facing its own challenges at home. history.descriptionZh:
美国对华AI芯片出口管制执法再度出现关键进展。第三方经纪人和“中间人”孙廷伟（Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun）已就相关指控认罪。他被控与美超微（Super Micro）联合创始人廖益贤（Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw）以及销售经理张瑞仓（Ruei-Tsang “Steven” Chang）共谋，将受出口管制的英伟达AI芯片非法转运至中国。根据彭博社报道，孙廷伟的认罪属于与检方达成协议的一部分，但是否包含配合调查、指证其他被告等安排，目前尚未披露。他预计将于2027年9月8日宣判。

案件背景是，美国近年来不断收紧对华先进AI芯片出口，试图在人工智能竞赛中维持对中国的硬件优势。今年早些时候，这起案件被曝光：涉案人员被指向东南亚公司运送装有英伟达芯片的美超微服务器，再由该公司伪造文件，并为检查人员制作假服务器。具体手法相当隐蔽：工人用吹风机加热并移除真实服务器上的序列号标签，再将其贴到假服务器外壳上，以完成调包假象，而真正的服务器则被运往中国。进一步调查显示，三人利用一家位于泰国的公司接收服务器，随后将其交付给阿里巴巴。不过，阿里巴巴否认收到被禁止的英伟达硬件。

从所谓“技术原理”看，本案并不涉及芯片性能或架构创新，关键点在于规避出口管制的物流与欺诈手法：利用东南亚中转、伪造报关和检查材料、制作假服务器、转移序列号，从而让真实AI服务器在形式上“消失”并流入中国。这类手法针对的是海关和出口合规检查，而不是芯片本身的技术突破。涉案产品包括英伟达AI芯片及相关服务器，台湾方面后续案件还涉及英伟达B300 GPU，但新闻未披露具体算力、显存、互联带宽等性能参数。

在法律和商业层面，美超微否认对相关操作知情，但报道称该操作自2024年以来已带来25亿美元销售额。公司股东已起诉美超微，指控其隐瞒对中国非法销售的依赖。廖益贤对指控不认罪，并以500万美元保释，预计今年11月2日受审；第三名被告张瑞仓仍在逃。台湾当局也在构建自己的案件，调查人员曾突袭美超微部分办公室和六名个人住所。美超微否认办公室被突袭，称公司配合警方并提供被调查员工的工作站和设备访问权限，同时表示正与美国和台湾当局合作调查，并在完成独立调查后解雇数名员工。随后，台湾又起诉另外九名涉嫌非法走私英伟达B300 GPU的人员。孙廷伟认罪是美国打击非法AI芯片出口的最新进展。此前，加州一名科技公司CEO也因涉嫌向中国走私价值3亿美元的英伟达AI服务器被捕，最高可能面临20年监禁。

这些案件表明，美国白宫和执法机构正以刑事起诉、出口管制和供应链审查等方式，严防先进AI硬件流入中国。其技术影响和应用场景主要围绕AI数据中心、大模型训练与推理等高性能算力需求展开：英伟达AI芯片和集成GPU的服务器是当前AI基础设施的核心，因此成为出口管制和走私争夺的焦点。对相关企业而言，这意味着更严格的合规审计、序列号追踪、转口贸易审查和内部治理要求；对AI产业而言，则可能进一步加剧先进算力获取的地缘政治分化。

history.titleZh: 本周 Tom's Hardware 高级版：2026年10月10日
history.descriptionZh:
本周 Tom's Hardware Premium 周报围绕一个核心趋势展开：AI 的算力扩张正在同时改变芯片需求、设计方式、供应链、能源消耗和地缘政治格局。以下为本周重点内容。

**AI 数据中心电力瓶颈：软件优化或成最容易的突破口**  
随着 AI 数据中心规模迅速膨胀，电力供应正成为超大规模云厂商最紧迫的约束之一。研究人员指出，智能软件利用可能是缓解 AI 电力紧张最容易实现的方案。报告援引专家访谈称，到 2030 年，全球数据中心用电需求预计将可与日本全国用电量相匹敌。这意味着，除了新建电厂和电网，如何通过软件调度、负载编排、动态功耗管理和利用率优化来降低单位算力能耗，将成为 AI 基础设施竞争的关键环节。

**腾讯与 Oracle 达成 70 亿美元 AI 芯片租赁协议，或成出口管制“租赁漏洞”**  
报道称，腾讯已与 Oracle 达成协议，将在五年内租赁价值 70 亿美元的高性能 AI 芯片，涉及约 10 万颗芯片。虽然总金额巨大，但估算显示，其每小时租赁价格约为 1.6 美元，比 Nvidia H100 一年期合同每小时 2.80 美元的标准租金低约 43%。尽管协议未点名具体芯片型号，但交易规模和价格指向 Hopper 级 GPU。  
这一安排的关键背景是美国对华先进 AI 芯片出口管制。中国企业直接购买受控硬件受限，但通过海外云厂商租赁算力，可能形成规避管制的“租赁漏洞”。若该模式被广泛采用，中国 AI 公司可在境外获得先进训练和推理算力，同时 Oracle 等云厂商获得大额收入，但也会引发更严格的监管审查。该交易因此不仅是商业租赁，更涉及出口管制有效性和全球 AI 算力地缘政治。

**OpenAI 与 Synopsys 合作构建“GPT-Synopsys”，推动自主芯片设计**  
Synopsys 本周公布多项新协议，其中最受关注的是与 OpenAI 的合作：双方将推出“GPT-Synopsys”，一个结合 Synopsys 领域 IP 知识、EDA 工具与 OpenAI 大语言模型设计能力的专用 AI 模型。它很可能是面向芯片制造的专用 AI 模型，并可能参与 OpenAI“Jalapeño”AI ASIC 后继产品的开发。  
核心技术逻辑在于：AI 模型设计芯片通常会遇到 IP 使用和工具链权限的障碍；如果 AI 实验室与 IP/EDA 厂商合作，这些障碍可被消除。GPT-Synopsys 可操作 EDA 工具，帮助工程师更快交付更复杂的芯片，推动芯片设计走向“代理化”未来。其应用场景包括芯片架构探索、RTL 生成、验证、物理设计等 EDA 流程的自动化。

**氖气回收系统上线：DUV 光刻供应链的救生索**  
氖气是一种惰性气体，广泛用于 DUV 光刻工艺，全球超过 70% 的氖供应被较老的光刻机消耗。粗氖生产通常集中在乌克兰，俄乌冲突爆发后全球供应受到严重扰乱。为此，日本光刻工具制造商 Gigaphoton 与竞争对手 Kanten Techno 竞相推出氖气回收系统。Gigaphoton 声称其系统可实现 50% 的回收率。  
技术原理是从 DUV 设备废气中回收氖气，经过纯化后重新用于光刻激光气体混合物。由于 DUV 仍是中国芯片制造生态的主要依赖，而 EUV 对氖的需求相对有限，氖回收系统对依赖 DUV 的芯片制造商具有重要供应安全意义，可缓解供应链风险并降低材料成本。

**高通获华为 LogicFolding 芯片堆叠专利许可，专利关系历史性反转**  
报道称，高通已与华为达成协议，将获得华为 LogicFolding 芯片架构相关专利许可，交易还涵盖 AI、网络、计算等技术领域的产品。LogicFolding 是一种芯片堆叠方法，核心目标是实现更快的数据传输，作为无法获得最先进 EUV 光刻机的一种替代路径。其许多技术思路与芯片行业已有做法相似，但华为已将其用于 Kirin 9050 Pro，拆解显示其下层 die 主要是缓存和 I/O。  
这一交易引人注目之处在于历史性反转：过去两家公司的专利许可主要是华为向高通支付专利费，而此次是高通获得华为专利许可。若交易获批，说明先进封装和芯片堆叠技术在地缘政治限制下的战略价值进一步上升，也可能影响未来 AI、网络和计算芯片的设计路线。

**Groq 前员工起诉董事会：200 亿美元 Nvidia 交易引发股东诉讼**  
两名前 Groq 员工和股东对 Groq 前董事会及 CEO 提起拟议集体诉讼，指控董事会违反职责，在 2025 年 12 月 Groq 与 Nvidia 达成 200 亿美元交易后导致股东损失数十亿美元。该交易并非正式收购，Nvidia 也不是被告，但据报道，绝大多数 Groq 员工已直接加入 Nvidia。Groq3 LPU 已在 Nvidia Vera Rubin 生态中展示并正在爬坡，Nvidia 的 Groq 3 LPX 计划于 2026 年下半年随 Vera Rubin 出货。  
原告称，董事会实际上把 LPU 技术和团队交给了 Nvidia，却让其他股东未能分享数十亿美元价值。此案凸显 AI 芯片初创公司在与巨头进行“非收购式”人才和技术整合时的治理与法律风险。

**Mistral 发布万亿参数 Large 4：欧洲最佳，但仍落后中国开源模型**  
欧洲公司 Mistral 发布 Large 4，也称 ML4，社媒上称“Le Chonk”。这是一个万亿参数模型。开放权重模型竞赛长期由美国或中国实验室主导，因此欧洲推出有竞争力的模型具有标志意义。测试机构 Artificial Analysis 给 ML4 的总体智能指数为 38 分，表现尚可，但仍落后于多个中国模型，包括 Kimi K3（max）、GLM-5.3-Flash 和 MiMo-V2.6.Pro。  
不过，ML4 在网络安全任务上表现突出，仅少数模型超过它。总体来看，欧洲主权 AI 努力虽取得明显进展，仍在追赶中国开源模型。Mistral 预计将在 10 月底前发布 ML4 的精确权重，全球闭源与开放权重模型的竞赛仍将继续。

综合来看，本周新闻共同显示：AI 已不只是芯片的应用场景，而是重塑芯片设计、制造、供应链、能源和法律格局的核心变量。

history.title: Senate investigation says that some AI data center claims are misleading
history.description: A Senate investigation on AI data centers question that costs and benefits that AI hyperscalers show when they apply for permits to put up their developments. The report says that these claims are misleading and that they don't show the real impact of these sites on the local economy.
history.content: Copy link Facebook X Whatsapp Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 6 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter The U.S. Senate has been conducting a year-long investigation into AI data centers, and its findings suggest that some developers have been misleading the public about the costs and benefits that these projects bring to their communities. According to Time, data center developers have routinely pointed to the number of construction jobs that projects bring to neighborhoods, but many have allegedly refused to share the number of permanent positions these projects bring to the neighborhood once they’ve reached operational status. A few companies that did give numbers point to a ratio of one permanent position for every megawatt of capacity, meaning a 100-megawatt development, which consumes around the same amount of electricity as 100,000 homes, would only hire 100 people.Go deeper with TH Premium: AI and data centers (Image credit: Microsoft)The data center cooling state of playThe custom AI ASIC state of play America’s AI chip rules keep changing — and the rest of the world is paying the priceGTC 2026: Ian Buck press Q&A transcript — VP of Hyperscale and HPC speaks out on shelving CPX and shipping LPU decode this yearDemand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsible“Congress must hold Big Tech accountable so these companies pay their fair share,” Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) told the publication. Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) also said, “This report lays bare what we have long known: working Americans and local communities are footing the bill for Big Tech’s massive expansion of data centers, while these companies continue to operate without transparency.”Aside from the lack of permanent jobs, the authorities also looked at the tax incentives these companies have been getting from local and state governments. The investigation revealed that although property-tax breaks catch critics’ attention during the application process, sales-tax exemptions on computer equipment are reportedly more lucrative, especially as these sites maintain, replace, and upgrade their hardware. The report estimated that 39% of a 1GW data center’s spending is allocated towards expensive GPUs, so if the data centers do not deliver the jobs and economic benefits they’ve promised, then the state is losing out on a lot of revenue.Latest Videos FromTom's HardwareWatch full video here: The investigation also revealed that the surveyed companies — Amazon, Google, Meta, Microsoft, CoreWeave, Digital Realty, and Equinix — don’t want to cover the costs of the additional infrastructure needed to serve their data centers even though they previously promised to “pay their own way.” While the companies said that they were willing to pay for direct costs, they argued that they should not be responsible for the larger investments that could potentially benefit other customers, such as new power plants and transmission lines, even though these were primarily driven by their power demands.There have already been efforts to legislate the ratepayer protection pledge that data center developers signed earlier this year, but it has failed because senators thought that it was “toothless.” This investigation shows that Congress is not giving up and that it’s conducting an even broader effort to regulate the infrastructure behind AI, especially with regard to its massive power consumption and other issues that residents living around them have been protesting against.
